blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Concrete Driveway Cost in Torquay in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to concrete driveway costs in Torquay, including pricing factors, finish options, and what to expect from your Surf Coast concreter.
body: If you are planning a new concrete driveway in Torquay, understanding the cost is the first step toward making an informed decision. In 2026, most homeowners across the Surf Coast can expect to pay between $4,500 and $12,000 for a standard residential driveway, depending on the size, finish, and site conditions. Factors like access to your property, the slope of your land, and the type of concrete finish you choose all play a significant role in the final price. At Pro Concreting, we provide detailed, fixed quotes that break down every cost element — no surprises, no hidden charges, just honest pricing for Torquay locals.

The size of your driveway is the single biggest cost driver. A standard single-car driveway in Torquay typically measures around 3 metres by 6 metres, totalling 18 square metres, while a double driveway can stretch to 6 metres by 6 metres or more. At current rates, plain concrete driveways in the Surf Coast region generally start from around $60 to $80 per square metre for the basics, while premium finishes like exposed aggregate or stamped concrete can push that figure to $100 to $150 per square metre. Site access also matters — if heavy machinery cannot easily reach your front yard, additional labour and equipment costs may apply to your Torquay project.

Your choice of concrete finish has a major impact on the total cost of your Torquay driveway. Plain broom-finished concrete remains the most affordable option, offering a clean, functional surface at a competitive price. Exposed aggregate — extremely popular across the Surf Coast for its durability and visual appeal — adds approximately 20 to 40 percent to the base cost but delivers a premium, slip-resistant surface that handles Torquay's sandy conditions beautifully. Coloured and stamped concrete options fall somewhere in between, offering aesthetic versatility. When choosing your finish, consider both your budget and the coastal environment, as some finishes require more maintenance in salt-air conditions.

Living in Torquay means your driveway needs to cope with specific coastal conditions that inland areas simply do not face. The salt-laden air, sandy soil profiles common across the Surf Coast, and Victoria's variable rainfall all influence the type of concrete mix and reinforcement your driveway requires. At Pro Concreting, we use marine-grade admixtures and steel reinforcement designed for coastal environments, ensuring your driveway withstands the elements for decades. The sandy soils around Torquay and Waurn Ponds also require proper base preparation — often involving compaction and the addition of crushed rock — to prevent settling and cracking over time.

When you receive a quote from a reputable Torquay concreter like Pro Concreting, it should include several key elements: site preparation and excavation, the concrete supply and delivery, steel reinforcement, formwork, finishing, and curing. A professional quote will also account for any necessary drainage solutions — critical in Torquay where winter rainfall can be heavy and persistent. Beware of quotes that seem unusually cheap, as they often exclude essential steps like proper ground compaction or adequate steel mesh. We believe in full transparency, which is why every Pro Concreting quote itemises each component so you know exactly what you are paying for.

To get the best value for your concrete driveway in Torquay, start by getting at least two to three detailed quotes from local, licensed concreters. Ask about the concrete mix specifications, reinforcement details, and what warranty or guarantee is offered on the finished product. Timing can also affect cost — scheduling your project during spring or early autumn typically allows for optimal curing conditions on the Surf Coast, potentially reducing the risk of weather delays. At Pro Concreting, we have been pouring driveways across Torquay and the greater Geelong region since 2005, and we are always happy to provide a free, no-obligation quote tailored to your specific project needs.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Pour Concrete on the Surf Coast: A Seasonal Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the ideal seasons for pouring concrete in Torquay and the Surf Coast, including weather tips and curing advice from local experts.
body: Timing is everything when it comes to pouring concrete, and nowhere is this more true than on Victoria's Surf Coast. Torquay's maritime climate brings cool, damp winters and warm, sometimes dry summers — both of which present unique challenges for concrete placement and curing. The ideal window for pouring concrete in Torquay generally falls between October and April, when daytime temperatures sit comfortably between 15 and 30 degrees Celsius. However, even within this window, local conditions like coastal winds, morning dew, and sudden weather changes require careful planning. At Pro Concreting, we have spent over 20 years working with the Surf Coast's weather patterns, scheduling pours for optimal results every time.

Summer in Torquay, running from December to February, offers the warmest conditions for concrete work, but it is not without its pitfalls. While the heat accelerates curing, temperatures above 35 degrees can cause the surface to dry too quickly, leading to surface cracking and reduced overall strength. The strong coastal winds that sweep through Torquay and Jan Juc can exacerbate this rapid evaporation from the surface. Experienced concreters like the Pro Concreting team counter this by scheduling early morning pours, using curing compounds, and covering fresh concrete with hessian or plastic sheeting to retain moisture. If you are planning a summer project in Torquay, book well in advance, as the best concreting contractors fill up quickly during the warm months.

Autumn and spring are widely considered the sweet spot for concrete pouring on the Surf Coast. From March to May and September to November, Torquay typically experiences moderate temperatures between 12 and 22 degrees, with lower wind speeds and more consistent humidity — all ideal conditions for even curing. These shoulder seasons give concrete the time it needs to cure properly without the extremes of summer heat or winter cold. Many of our clients at Pro Concreting schedule their driveway and patio projects during these periods specifically because the results tend to be more consistent and reliable. If your timeline allows, aiming for an autumn or spring pour in Torquay is always a smart move.

Winter concrete pours in Torquay, from June through August, require extra caution but are not impossible. The Surf Coast's winters bring temperatures that can drop below 5 degrees overnight, which significantly slows the curing process and can compromise strength if the concrete freezes before it has adequately set. Rainfall also increases during these months, and wet conditions can delay pours or affect the finish quality. If a winter pour is necessary, experienced Torquay concreters use insulated blankets, accelerators in the concrete mix, and careful timing to ensure the pour happens during the warmest part of the day. Pro Concreting has successfully managed winter projects across the Surf Coast by planning meticulously around the forecast.

Beyond seasonal timing, several Torquay-specific factors influence when and how you should pour concrete. The proximity to the coast means higher humidity levels, which can actually benefit curing by slowing moisture loss from the surface naturally. However, the sandy soils prevalent across Torquay, Waurn Ponds, and Mount Duneed can drain quickly, potentially wicking moisture away from fresh concrete if the sub-base is not properly prepared. Morning dew is common on the Surf Coast, even in warmer months, so timing your pour to avoid placing concrete on wet surfaces is important. Understanding these micro-climate factors is what separates a good concrete finish from a great one, and it is something the Pro Concreting team considers for every Torquay project.

The bottom line for Torquay homeowners is that planning your concrete project around the best seasonal window will save you money and deliver a better, longer-lasting result. Whether you are pouring a new driveway in Ceres, a patio in Jan Juc, or a commercial slab in Grovedale, working with a local concreter who understands the Surf Coast's unique conditions makes all the difference. At Pro Concreting, we monitor weather forecasts closely and communicate openly with our clients about the optimal timing for their specific project. Contact us for a free quote and we will help you plan the perfect pour for your Torquay property — whether that is in the mild days of autumn or the warmth of late spring.

blogPosts.title: Exposed Aggregate vs Coloured Concrete: Which Suits Your Torquay Home?
blogPosts.excerpt: Compare exposed aggregate and coloured concrete for your Torquay driveway or patio — durability, cost, aesthetics, and coastal performance.
body: Choosing between exposed aggregate and coloured concrete is one of the most common decisions Torquay homeowners face when planning a new driveway, patio, or path. Both finishes offer excellent durability and visual appeal, but they differ significantly in appearance, maintenance requirements, cost, and how they perform in the Surf Coast's coastal environment. Exposed aggregate has become the go-to choice for many Torquay properties, thanks to its textured, slip-resistant surface and natural stone look. Coloured concrete, on the other hand, offers a smoother, more uniform appearance with a wide palette of colour options. Understanding the differences will help you select the right finish for your home and your budget.

Exposed aggregate concrete is created by removing the top layer of cement paste to reveal the decorative stone aggregate beneath. This finish is incredibly popular in Torquay and across the Surf Coast because it combines aesthetic appeal with practical benefits that suit coastal living. The exposed stones provide natural slip resistance — essential around pool areas, sloped driveways, and entryways exposed to Torquay's coastal rain. The aggregate also hides minor surface imperfections and staining better than smoother finishes, making it ideal for high-traffic areas. With a wide variety of aggregate options available — from local river stones to imported decorative pebbles — you can customise the look to complement your Torquay home's style and surroundings perfectly.

Coloured concrete achieves its look through either integral colour mixed throughout the concrete batch or a surface-applied colour hardener during finishing. This option provides a clean, contemporary appearance that suits modern Torquay homes beautifully. The colour palette ranges from earthy terracotta and sandstone tones to sleek charcoals and slate greys — many of which echo the natural tones of the Surf Coast landscape. However, coloured concrete requires more careful maintenance than exposed aggregate, as surface colour can fade over time with UV exposure, particularly in Torquay's harsh summer sun. Applying a quality sealer every two to three years helps maintain vibrancy and protects the surface from salt air and staining.

When it comes to cost, exposed aggregate typically sits at the mid-to-upper range of concrete finishes, generally costing 20 to 40 percent more than plain broom-finished concrete. Coloured concrete falls into a similar price bracket, though the cost varies depending on whether you choose integral colour or surface-applied hardeners. Both options require skilled workmanship to achieve a professional result — exposed aggregate demands precise timing during the washing phase, while coloured concrete needs consistent and even application to avoid patchiness. In Torquay, most homeowners investing in a new driveway or outdoor area find that either finish adds significant value to their property, with exposed aggregate being the more popular choice for its longevity and low maintenance.

For Torquay's coastal environment, both finishes have specific considerations that are worth understanding before you commit. Exposed aggregate performs exceptionally well in salt-air conditions, as the natural stone is inherently resistant to corrosion and weathering over time. The textured surface also provides excellent grip when wet — a genuine safety benefit during Torquay's rainy winter months when paths and driveways become slippery. Coloured concrete, while equally durable structurally, may require more attention to surface sealing to prevent the colour from degrading in the coastal elements. The Surf Coast's sandy soils also mean that lighter-coloured concretes may show dirt and sand accumulation more readily. For this reason, many of our Torquay clients opt for mid-tone aggregates or colours that complement the natural sand and soil tones of the region.

So which should you choose for your Torquay property? If you prioritise low maintenance, slip resistance, and a textured natural look that hides everyday wear, exposed aggregate is likely your best bet — and it is the finish we recommend most often for Surf Coast driveways and pool surrounds. If you prefer a smooth, contemporary aesthetic and do not mind periodic resealing, coloured concrete offers stunning versatility. Ultimately, the right choice depends on your property's style, your budget, and how you use the space day to day. At Pro Concreting, we have installed both finishes extensively across Torquay, Waurn Ponds, and the greater Geelong region. Contact us for a free on-site consultation and we will help you choose the perfect finish for your home.

blogPosts.title: How to Choose the Right Concrete Finish for Your Torquay Pool Surround
blogPosts.excerpt: A Torquay homeowner's guide to selecting the safest, most durable concrete finish for your pool area, including coastal-specific advice.
body: A pool surround is one of the most important concrete projects a Torquay homeowner can undertake, and choosing the right finish is critical for both safety and aesthetics. With Torquay's outdoor lifestyle and warm Surf Coast summers, your pool area sees heavy foot traffic, constant water exposure, and direct sunlight — all of which demand a concrete finish that can handle the conditions year-round. The three most popular pool surround finishes in Torquay are exposed aggregate, stamped concrete, and plain broom-finished concrete, each with distinct advantages and trade-offs. At Pro Concreting, we have installed hundreds of pool surrounds across the Surf Coast, and we have seen firsthand which finishes perform best in our unique coastal environment.

Slip resistance should be your number one priority when selecting a pool surround finish in Torquay. Wet feet on smooth concrete create a genuine safety hazard, particularly for families with young children or elderly residents. Exposed aggregate excels in this department — the textured stone surface provides excellent grip even when completely wet, making it the safest and most popular option for pool areas across the Surf Coast. Stamped concrete can offer moderate slip resistance depending on the pattern selected, though it typically requires an anti-slip additive in the sealer to match exposed aggregate's natural performance. Plain broom-finished concrete with a heavy broom texture is another affordable option that provides adequate traction for Torquay pool surrounds.

Coastal durability is another major factor for Torquay pool surrounds that many homeowners initially overlook. Chlorinated pool water, combined with salt air carried in from the nearby coast, creates a harsh chemical environment that can degrade inferior concrete finishes over time. Exposed aggregate handles these conditions exceptionally well because the natural stones are inherently resistant to chemical attack and weathering. The cement matrix between the stones can be sealed with a penetrating sealer that adds an extra layer of protection against chlorine and salt exposure. Coloured and stamped concrete finishes, while attractive, may be more susceptible to surface erosion from pool chemicals if the sealer is not maintained on a regular schedule.

Aesthetics play a big role in your decision too — your pool surround should complement your Torquay home and the natural coastal landscape surrounding it. Exposed aggregate offers a beachy, organic look that blends seamlessly with the Surf Coast environment and pairs beautifully with native coastal plantings. Popular aggregate choices for Torquay pool areas include light-coloured quartz and river pebbles that reflect the sandy tones of nearby beaches. Stamped concrete can replicate the appearance of natural stone, slate, or tile, offering a more structured and contemporary look that suits modern Torquay homes. The key is choosing a colour and texture that will not show every footprint or water mark — something the Pro Concreting team can advise on during your free on-site consultation at your Torquay property.

Drainage is often overlooked but absolutely critical for a Torquay pool surround. Proper falls and gradients ensure water drains away from your pool and house, preventing pooling, slippery surfaces, and potential water damage to adjacent structures and foundations. The Surf Coast experiences significant rainfall during the winter months, so a well-designed drainage system — including slot drains or strip drains where needed — is essential for any pool area. When planning your pool surround with a Torquay concreter, discuss drainage requirements early in the design process rather than as an afterthought. Pro Concreting integrates drainage solutions into every pool surround project, ensuring compliance with Australian standards while maintaining the visual appeal of your finished surface.

Budgeting for your Torquay pool surround should account for both the initial installation cost and the long-term maintenance expenses over its lifetime. While exposed aggregate may cost more upfront than plain broom-finished concrete, its superior durability and lower maintenance requirements often make it more economical over a 15 to 20 year period. Sealing costs for pool surrounds in the Surf Coast typically range from $3 to $6 per square metre every two to three years, depending on the finish type and exposure conditions. At Pro Concreting, we provide transparent, itemised quotes for pool surround projects across Torquay, Jan Juc, Waurn Ponds, and all surrounding Surf Coast suburbs. Contact us for a free consultation and we will help you design a pool surround that is safe, stunning, and built to last in Torquay's demanding coastal conditions.
